hints: Work backwards from the cyanohydrin, remember only aldehydes and ketones react with HCN to form them.
Draw out 2-hydroxybutanenitrile as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$ and ask what $\text{C=O}$ compound it must have come from.
Once you have identified propanal as the carbonyl intermediate, think which type of alcohol gives an aldehyde on mild oxidation.
walkthrough:
**Find the carbonyl compound that makes the cyanohydrin**

Think of HCN addition as adding H to the oxygen and CN to the carbon of a $\text{C=O}$ bond. So strip the $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CN}$ from the same carbon and put back $\text{=O}$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN} \text{ comes from } \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$$

**Name that carbonyl compound**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ has 3 carbons with an $\text{-CHO}$ group, so it is propanal, an aldehyde. This must be one product of oxidising X.

**Link aldehyde back to the alcohol X**

Recall the mild oxidation rules. Primary alcohol gives aldehyde, secondary alcohol gives ketone, tertiary gives no reaction.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{aldehyde} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{carboxylic acid}$$

$$\text{secondary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{ketone}$$

**Identify X**

Since we need propanal, X must be the primary alcohol with the same 3-carbon skeleton. That is propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.

options.A: Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol so it oxidises to butanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. With HCN this would give 2-hydroxypentanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$, which has 5 carbons, not 4.
options.B: Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol so it oxidises to the ketone butanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. With HCN this would give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_3$, a branched cyanohydrin, not 2-hydroxybutanenitrile.
options.C: Propan-1-ol is a primary alcohol and is mildly oxidised to propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. Propanal then undergoes nucleophilic addition with HCN to give exactly $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$, 2-hydroxybutanenitrile.
options.D: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol so it oxidises to propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. With HCN this would give 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanenitrile, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C(OH)CN}$, which is branched and different from the straight-chain product required.
